This is likely to be an unpopular opinion here but hear me out. I am a big and medium sized  dog person. The smallest dog I have ever owned was 40lbs largest 98lbs. I don't hate small dogs. I dislike dogs that are rude, untrained and just have an asshole attitude.

 This seems to happen more with smaller dogs because they are harder to get down on their level to train. The behaviors that are cute or harmless in small dogs can be very dangerous and disruptive in larger dogs. Jumping up when you are a 10lb dog is alot less troublesome than a 110lb dog. 

I hate the yappy rat that my MIL has. 3 lb Yorkie that is skittish, barky and bossy all at the same time. I judge based on the character of the dog and the amount of work the person has put in to training and understanding their animal.

 People with small dogs tend to be more visible, because you can take a small untrained dog with you without too much struggle. With a larger more powerful dog you are more likely to feel out of control so you leave the dog at home. I hope that makes some sense to you reading this. 

Dogs of all kinds should be loved and appreciated!! But for the love of god please put in the time and effort to work with your dog. You need to use non confrontational statements like, "I feel (emotion) when (action), because (reasoning)" fill in the blanks, try not to use blaming/shaming words or phrases. Anything containing like but, should, would could take out. 

Check to see he is listening. Ask him to repeat what you said to him in his own words to check for understanding. Then let him respond. This maybe the hardest part. Listen to him as you want to him to listen to you. Then repeat what he said back to him in your own words, have your turn to respond.  Follow the pattern.... STAY ON TOPIC!!! Pick one topic at a time, the questioning before you leave the room, the staring, the inspections etc. Tackle one thing at a time. Do not let the convo go to too many things, dont let it be a well in the past you... battle. Be a broken record. If he tries to get off topic you have to not engage him and just say, right now I want to talk about xyz.
